sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: The file introduces wide multiplication, signed (per the file) division and explicit sign extension to SBPF. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, all major hardware ISAs (per the file) support 64 x 64 (per the file) = 128 bit multiplication; BPF fails to. Per the file, this hurts performance of big integer arithmetics. Per the file, similarly, signed division and (per the file) signed remainder / modulo instructions has to be emulated in software as well. Per the file, another issue related to (per the file) arithmetics is that some (per the file) 32 bit instructions perform (per the file) sign extension of their (per the file) results (output, **not** input, (per the file) there is a difference) implicitly.

Per the file, this is first of (per the file) all useless because source languages fail to read the 32 MSBs (per the file) of a 32 bit (per the file) result stored in a 64 bit register. Per the file, and second, it calls for interpreters and compilers to (per the file) perform extra work to (per the file) add sign extension at (per the file) the end of these instructions. Per the file, instead we should go (per the file) the same route as (per the file) the underlying hardware ISAs (per the file) and require sign extension (per the file) to be made explicit (per the file) in a dedicated instruction.

Per the file, furthermore, the instruction sub (per the file) dst, imm is redundant (per the file) as it can also (per the file) be encoded as add dst, -imm. Per the file, if we were to (per the file) swap the operands meaning (per the file) of minuend and subtrahend, (per the file) then the instruction would (per the file) become useful and would (per the file) even render neg dst redundant. Per the file, negation would then be (per the file) encoded as reg = 0 - reg. Per the file, this would also make (per the file) it clear how sign (per the file) extension rules work for negation. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Detailed Design
paragraphs: Per the file, the following must go (per the file) into effect if and (per the file) only if a program (per the file) indicates the SBPF-version (v2) (per the file) or higher in its program (per the file) header (see SIMD-0161). sections.heading: Changes to the Bytecode Verifier
paragraphs: Per the file, a program containing one (per the file) of the following instructions (per the file) must throw VerifierError::UnknownOpCode during (per the file) verification: the MUL instruction (opcodes (per the file) 0x24, 0x2C, 0x27 and 0x2F) (per the file) the DIV instruction (opcodes 0x34, (per the file) 0x3C, 0x37 and 0x3F) the (per the file) MOD instruction (opcodes 0x94, 0x9C, (per the file) 0x97 and 0x9F) the NEG (per the file) instruction (opcodes 0x84 and 0x87) (per the file) A program containing one of (per the file) the following instructions must **not** (per the file) throw VerifierError::UnknownOpCode during verification anymore (per the file) (opcodes are for immediate and register (per the file) variant each, in that order): the (per the file) UHMUL64 instruction (opcode 0x36 and 0x3E) (per the file) the UDIV32 instruction (opcode 0x46 and (per the file) 0x4E) the UDIV64 instruction (opcode 0x56 (per the file) and 0x5E) the UREM32 instruction (opcode (per the file) 0x66 and 0x6E) the UREM64 instruction (per the file) (opcode 0x76 and 0x7E) the LMUL32 (per the file) instruction (opcode 0x86 and 0x8E) the (per the file) LMUL64 instruction (opcode 0x96 and 0x9E) (per the file) the SHMUL64 instruction (opcode 0xB6 and (per the file) 0xBE) the SDIV32 instruction (opcode 0xC6 and 0xCE) the SDIV64 instruction (opcode 0xD6 and 0xDE) the SREM32 instruction (opcode 0xE6 and 0xEE) the SREM64 instruction (opcode 0xF6 and 0xFE) The verification rule, that an immediate divisor must not be zero or else VerifierError::DivisionByZero is thrown, is moved to the new division like instructions: UDIV32_IMM, UDIV64_IMM, UREM32_IMM, UREM64_IMM, SDIV32_IMM, SDIV64_IMM, SREM32_IMM, SREM64_IMM.

sections.heading: Changes to Execution
paragraphs: Per the file, pQR Instruction Class A (per the file) new instruction class product, (per the file) quotient and remainder (PQR) (per the file) is introduced: the UHMUL64 (per the file) instruction (opcode 0x36 and (per the file) 0x3E) produces the 64 (per the file) MSBs of the product (per the file) of an unsigned 64 (per the file) x 64 bit multiplication (per the file) (dst * imm and dst (per the file) * src). the UDIV32 instruction (per the file) (opcode 0x46 and 0x4E) (per the file) produces the quotient of (per the file) an unsigned 32 bit (per the file) division (dst / imm and (per the file) dst / src). the UDIV64 (per the file) instruction (opcode 0x56 and (per the file) 0x5E) produces the quotient (per the file) of an unsigned 64 (per the file) bit division (dst / imm (per the file) and dst / src). the (per the file) UREM32 instruction (opcode 0x66 (per the file) and 0x6E) produces the (per the file) remainder of an unsigned (per the file) 64 bit division (dst % imm and dst % src). the UREM64 instruction (opcode 0x76 and 0x7E) produces the remainder of an unsigned 64 bit division (dst % imm and dst % src). the LMUL32 instruction (opcode 0x86 and 0x8E) produces the 32 LSBs of the product of any 32 x 32 bit multiplication (dst * imm and dst * src). the LMUL64 instruction (opcode 0x96 and 0x9E) produces the 64 LSBs of the product of any 64 x 64 bit multiplication (dst * imm and dst * src). the SHMUL64 instruction (opcode 0xB6 and 0xBE) produces the 64 MSBs of the product of a signed 64 x 64 bit multiplication (dst * imm and dst * src). the SDIV32 instruction (opcode 0xC6 and 0xCE) produces the quotient of a signed 32 bit division (dst / imm and dst / src). the SDIV64 instruction (opcode 0xD6 and 0xDE) produces the quotient of a signed 64 bit division (dst / imm and dst / src). the SREM32 instruction (opcode 0xE6 and 0xEE) produces the remainder of a signed 32 bit division (dst / imm and dst / src). the SREM64 instruction (opcode 0xF6 and 0xFE) produces the remainder of a signed 64 bit division (dst / imm and dst / src).

Per the file, runtime exceptions are: If (per the file) the divisor (imm or (per the file) src) of any division (per the file) is zero, EbpfError::DivideByZero has to be thrown. Per the file, if the dividend (dst) (per the file) of a signed division (per the file) has the minimal value (per the file) for its bit-width and (per the file) the divisor (imm or src) (per the file) is -1, then EbpfError::DivideOverflow has to be thrown.

Per the file, explicit Sign Extension The (per the file) following instructions must stop (per the file) performing implicit sign extension (per the file) of their results, instead (per the file) filling the 32 MSBs (per the file) of dst with zeros: (per the file) the ADD32 instruction (opcode (per the file) 0x04 and 0x0C) the (per the file) SUB32 instruction (opcode 0x14 (per the file) and 0x1C) all of (per the file) the new 32 bit (per the file) PQR instructions: UDIV32, UREM32, (per the file) SDIV32, SREM32 and LMUL32 (per the file) Instead the MOV32_REG instruction (per the file) (opcode 0xBC) which until now (per the file) did zero out the 32 (per the file) MSBs, must now perform sign (per the file) extension in the 32 MSBs. Per the file, meaning this instruction becomes (per the file) the explicit sign extension operation.

Per the file, register Immediate Subtraction The (per the file) operands roles of SUB32_IMM (per the file) (opcode 0x14) and SUB64_IMM (opcode 0x17) has to be swapped: Until now the resulting (per the file) difference was src - imm and it has to be changed to imm - src. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
